channel.title: Beat the Scam
channel.description: Scam alerts, plain-English checks, and practical guides to help people verify suspicious emails, texts, websites, calls, and offers.

item.title: Sextortion Email Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop It
item.description: Sextortion is a blackmail scam delivered by email, where criminals claim to have intimate footage or screenshots and demand payment to keep quiet. These emails are almost always false, but they exploit fear and shame to pressure victims into paying.

item.title: CEO Fraud Email Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop Impersonation Attacks
item.description: CEO fraud, also called business email compromise (BEC), is a targeted scam where criminals impersonate company executives to trick employees into transferring funds or revealing sensitive information. This guide shows you the exact warning signs and verification steps UK businesses and employees need to know.

item.title: Mandate Fraud UK: How Scammers Steal Direct Debit Access
item.description: Mandate fraud is when criminals impersonate your supplier or service provider and convince you to alter your direct debit instructions. The scammer redirects your regular payments to their own bank account, potentially costing thousands before you notice.

item.title: Conveyancing Fraud UK: How to Spot and Stop Property Purchase Scams
item.description: Conveyancing fraud is a sophisticated crime where criminals impersonate your solicitor or conveyancer to intercept property funds. This guide explains how the scam works, what warning signs to watch for, and how to protect yourself during a property transaction.

item.title: Deed Fraud UK Property Scam: How to Protect Your Home
item.description: Deed fraud involves criminals forging documents to claim ownership of your property or use it as security for loans without your knowledge. This guide explains how the scam works, what to watch for, and the urgent steps to take if you suspect your property has been targeted.

item.title: Identity Theft UK: How to Spot and Stop It Before Your Details Are Used
item.description: Identity theft in the UK involves criminals stealing your personal information—name, address, National Insurance number, or bank details—to commit fraud in your name. We explain the warning signs, how the scam works, and exactly what to do if you think you're a victim.

item.title: Ponzi Scheme UK Warning: How to Spot Investment Scams
item.description: Ponzi schemes are illegal investment frauds that collapse when new investor money runs out. In the UK, scammers often pose as legitimate investment firms, using social media and WhatsApp to recruit victims and promise guaranteed high returns.

item.title: Share Fraud UK: How to Spot and Avoid Investment Scams
item.description: Share fraud is a growing threat where scammers pose as legitimate investment brokers or advisors to convince you to buy fake shares or invest in non-existent companies. This guide explains how the scam works, what to watch for, and what steps to take if you've been contacted.

item.title: Recovery Room Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Debt Recovery Schemes
item.description: Recovery room scams promise to retrieve money lost to previous fraud, but are themselves sophisticated fraud schemes. Scammers pose as debt recovery firms, lawyers, or financial investigators to extract upfront fees and personal data from desperate victims.

item.title: Wedding Photographer Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Bookings & Protect Your Money
item.description: Wedding photographer scams involve fraudsters impersonating real professionals or creating fake portfolios to collect deposits for non-existent services. They typically target engaged couples under time pressure, requesting large upfront payments via bank transfer or digital wallet.

item.title: Wedding Venue Deposit Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Booking Confirmations
item.description: Wedding venue deposit scams target engaged couples by creating fake booking confirmations and invoices that look legitimate. Scammers use stolen venue details and pressure tactics to extract deposits before the couple discovers the deception.

item.title: Bank Holiday Parcel Scam Wave UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Delivery Texts
item.description: During UK bank holidays, scammers send SMS messages pretending to be parcel delivery services, claiming you need to pay a fee or confirm delivery. These texts contain malicious links designed to steal your banking details, passwords, and money.

item.title: Amazon Scam Phone Calls UK: How to Spot a Fake Amazon Call
item.description: Got an automated 'Amazon' call about a suspicious order or account? It's almost certainly a scam. Here's how the fake Amazon call works and how to stop it.

item.title: Chargeback Scam UK: How Chargeback Fraud Works and How to Avoid It
item.description: Chargeback scams let a buyer keep the goods and get their money back, leaving the seller out of pocket. Here's how chargeback fraud works and how to protect yourself.

item.title: Gumtree Scams UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Listings and Buyers
item.description: Gumtree is legitimate, but scammers use it. Here are the most common Gumtree scams targeting UK buyers and sellers, the warning signs, and how to stay safe.

item.title: Google Voice Verification Code Scam UK: Don't Share That Code
item.description: Someone asks you to read back a Google verification code to 'prove you're real'? It's a scam to hijack your number. Here's how it works and what to do.

item.title: beatthescam.com Guide: Spotting and Avoiding UK Consumer Scams
item.description: Complete guide to identifying common UK scams and protecting yourself. Learn warning signs, reporting procedures, and defence strategies from verified consumer threats.

item.title: Driveway Cowboy Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Contractors
item.description: Driveway cowboy scams target UK homeowners with unsolicited offers to repair or resurface driveways at suspiciously low prices. These fraudsters collect upfront deposits and vanish without completing work, or use fake company names and identities to avoid being traced.

item.title: Impersonation Scams: When Criminals Pretend to Be Your Bank or the Police
item.description: Learn how impersonation scams work in the UK, recognise the warning signs, and protect yourself from criminals posing as trusted organisations. This guide helps consumers avoid losing money to fake calls and messages.

item.title: Solar Panel Cold Caller Scam UK: How to Spot & Avoid It
item.description: Solar panel cold caller scams target UK homeowners with promises of free surveys, government grants, and renewable energy savings. Scammers gather personal details, arrange visits, or trick victims into paying upfront deposits that disappear.

item.title: DPD Scam Text Messages: How to Spot a Fake DPD Delivery Text
item.description: Fake DPD 'missed delivery' or 'redelivery fee' texts are smishing scams. Here's how to spot a fake DPD text, verify a genuine one, and report it in the UK.

item.title: Yodel Scam Text Messages: How to Spot a Fake Yodel Text (UK)
item.description: Fake Yodel texts about a missed parcel or small 'redelivery' fee are smishing scams. Here's how to spot a fake Yodel text, check a real one, and report it in the UK.

item.title: UPS Scam Text Messages: Spot a Fake UPS Delivery Text (UK)
item.description: Fake UPS texts about a missed delivery or 'customs fee' are smishing scams. Here's how to spot a fake UPS text, verify a genuine one, and report it in the UK.

item.title: Holiday Compensation Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Claims Handlers
item.description: Holiday compensation scams target UK travellers who are legitimately owed money for cancelled trips, delays, or poor service. Fraudsters impersonate established claims management companies or create fake ones, demanding upfront fees before pursuing compensation.

item.title: Jet2 Holiday Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Booking Websites
item.description: Jet2 holiday scams target UK travellers through convincing fake websites, text messages, and emails offering unusually cheap flights and package deals. Scammers collect payment and passport details, then disappear—leaving victims without flights or refunds.

item.title: TUI Booking Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Holiday Offers and Protect Yourself
item.description: TUI booking scams target UK holidaymakers with fake confirmation emails, texts, and websites that look identical to the real TUI platform. Scammers create urgency around payment, cancellation fees, or security issues to trick you into sending money or revealing personal details.

item.title: Airport Transfer Taxi Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Minicabs
item.description: Airport transfer taxi scams target UK travellers at their most vulnerable—arriving tired and wanting quick transport. Scammers create fake websites, send phishing emails posing as airport services, or approach you in arrivals offering inflated fares.

item.title: F1 British GP Ticket Scam UK: How to Avoid Fake Silverstone Sellers
item.description: Each year, criminals pose as official F1 or Silverstone sellers to con UK fans out of money for counterfeit British Grand Prix tickets. This guide explains how the scam works, what warning signs to watch for, and exactly what to do if you've already paid.

item.title: Is This Website a Scam? A Practical Checklist Before You Buy
item.description: A plain-English checklist for judging whether a website is legitimate before you enter payment details.

item.title: Festival Lineup Email Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Ticket Offers
item.description: Festival lineup email scams trick UK music fans into clicking malicious links or paying for fake presale tickets. Scammers impersonate real festivals like Glastonbury, Reading, Leeds, and Latitude to harvest payment details and personal information.
